title: SWETUGG 2015 - Is TDD Dead? What are the alternatives? - Emily Bache
summary: Emily Bache responds to the 'Is TDD dead' debate: TDD biases toward indirection, unit tests alone miss integration errors, and the pyramid ratios are beginner advice.

assertions.quote: tdd gives you a bias uh a bias towards in Direction and interfaces and all that

verdicts.note: Test-induced indirection is widely reported in practice and in the DHH debate, but controlled studies of TDD on design quality show small mixed effects.

Abstraction metrics (Martin's abstractness, interfaces, abstract classes) were higher for test-first projects in most of the six studies though not conclusively, and the test-first units carried more parameters and information flow; the same study found test-first classes smaller and less complex, so the harm to clarity was not observed.

assertions.quote: there are classes of defects that unit tests do not find kind of by definition they do not find integration errors

verdicts.note: By construction isolated unit tests do not exercise component interaction; integration failures are a well-documented defect class.

assertions.quote: the pyramid might not look like a pyramid it might it might actually look like you flipped it but that might be the right decision

verdicts.note: Reasonable and consistent with practice, but no study compares test-mix strategies against outcomes.

assertions.quote: it's actually very difficult to get the threading and the timing right for a machine to use the user interface
if you do them well they actually I think pay back very well in finding bugs often compared with unit tests

verdicts.note: Integration and system tests do catch defects unit tests miss, but relative cost-effectiveness depends on the system and is not well quantified.
